route_note: raft is header-only for select_k: our own driver.cu is compiled against the checkout's cpp/include (raft at the exact commit, placed FIRST on the include path; the kernel is raft/matrix/detail/select_radix.cuh, untouched). raft's headers are not self-contained, so the per-variant tarball (one gzip of 4 concatenated git-archive tar streams, unpacked by rw.sh with tar -xizf) also holds the pinned dependencies, identical for both variants: rmm 5fd6cee381d9 (cpp/include + cpp/src; the 41 src/*.cpp of rmm/cpp/CMakeLists.txt are compiled with g++ -std=c++17 -O3 -DNDEBUG -fPIC into libdeps.a), rapids-logger 4c72b598f99c (v0.2.3; include, src/logger.cpp, cmake/logger_macros.hpp.in), spdlog v1.14.1 (27cb4c76; compiled lib incl. its bundled fmt). Why these: rmm = 5fd6cee3 dated 2026-05-22, the buggy commit's date (pin chosen by the coordinator; not re-derived from rapids-cmake); rapids-logger = the revision rapids-cmake@a773bfa (main on 2026-05-22) pins in cpm/versions.json for rapids_logger, i.e. what raft's and rmm's CMake would fetch (NOT the newer b4bd48a, whose logger needs C++20 <format>, absent in the nodes' gcc 12.4); spdlog 1.14.1 is what that rapids-logger pins, and with its default (BUILD_SHARED_LIBS=ON -> RAPIDS_LOGGER_HIDE_ALL_SPDLOG_SYMBOLS=ON -> FMT_OPTION BUNDLED) spdlog uses its bundled fmt, so no external fmt is built (fmt 11.0.2 is only the pin of the EXTERNAL_FMT options, unused). CCCL, CUDA runtime and nvtx3 are the toolkit's (CUDA 13.4 ships CCCL; raft is not a CCCL target; RAFT_NVTX is OFF by default). The two CMake-generated headers raft/core/logger_macros.hpp and rmm/logger_macros.hpp are produced in t_build by the sed substitution that configure_file does on rapids-logger's cmake/logger_macros.hpp.in (prefix RAFT/RMM, default logger raft::default_logger()/rmm::default_logger()); version_config.hpp of raft/rmm is included by no header and not generated. Flags from raft's cpp/CMakeLists.txt + cmake/modules/ConfigureCUDA.cmake (Release): -std=c++17 (cxx_std_17/cuda_std_17), -O3 -DNDEBUG, --expt-extended-lambda --expt-relaxed-constexpr, -DRAFT_LOG_ACTIVE_LEVEL=RAPIDS_LOGGER_LOG_LEVEL_INFO, -DRAFT_SYSTEM_LITTLE_ENDIAN=1, -DCUDA_API_PER_THREAD_DEFAULT_STREAM, -DRAFT_HIDE_DEPRECATION_WARNINGS, plus -arch=sm_89 -lineinfo; NOT reproduced: -Werror/-Wall, fatbin compression (-Xfatbin=-compress-all, size only), OpenMP.
driver: driver.cu: raft::resources + raft::matrix::select_k<float,int64_t>(handle, device_matrix_view in (batch x len, row-major), nullopt, out_val, out_idx, select_min=true, sorted=false, SelectAlgo::kRadix8bits). Default: 2 rows x 50000 floats, k=64. This launches 4x radix_kernel<float,long,8,512,fused_last_filter=false (passes 0-2)/true (pass 3),dense_layout<long>> with grid (25,2) x 512 threads (nsys on the sm_75 smoke build lists exactly these: 3 instances of the <..,0> and 1 of the <..,1> instantiation, no radix_topk_one_block). Optional args: driver [batch] [len] [k] [algo 8|11|112] [iters]; algo 11 = kRadix11bits, 112 = kRadix11bitsExtraPass. The driver evaluates the dispatch condition itself (len > 512*32 = 16384 and impl::calc_grid_dim() > 1, the same function select_radix.cuh's select_k() uses) and prints calc_grid_dim; rc 3 if the one-block path would be taken. The result is checked against a host partial_sort reference (values and indices) and the line says OK or MISMATCH (rc stays 0; rc 2 = CUDA/raft error).
input: 2 x 50000 float keys = 100,000 elements (mt19937 seed 12345, random finite float bit patterns so the first 8-bit digit is spread over ~250 buckets and the histogram merge involves many warps), k=64, select_min. Thread-level access estimate (analytic, not measured; 25,600 threads per launch, 4 launches): pass 0 reads 100k elements with 128-bit loads (~25k global loads) + a shared atomic (LDS+ATOMS.CAST.SPIN, ~2 accesses) per element (~200k) + histogram merge 50 blocks x (256 LDS + <=256 global atomics) (~26k) -> ~0.26M; pass 1 same input read (~25k) + 3 counter loads per thread (~77k) + smem zero/merge (~38k) -> ~0.15M; passes 2 and 3 only the ~195 candidates per row but the same per-thread prologue and merge (~0.13M each). Total ~0.7M, bound ~2M, i.e. well under the 1e7 aim and the 1e8 limit.
